iterations.carryover: Iter-1 delivered the Tauri shell, Codex auth, streaming conversation UX, and app-server default runtime. Open carryover: app-server approvals/user input, real DOM/Vision/PTY providers, report/milestone files, and resident desktop ops.
openRisks: Codex app-server protocol is experimental; keep exec fallback available.
Browser store account submission is deferred until after dogfooding.

iterations.label: Durable Product State
iterations.goal: Build Codex Widget into a durable local-first desktop product with daemon-owned SQLite state, recoverable sessions, internal tabs, trash, artifact history, provider snapshots, activity logs, and extensible theme/mascot/module foundations.
iterations.carryover: Iter-2 completed the app-server runtime, reconnect replay, regenerate rollback, DOM/Vision/PTY providers, renderer chat hardening, release readiness gates, and resident desktop operations for dogfooding. Iter-3 carries forward the product owner request to route follow-up work through vibe-iterate and make daemon-owned durable product state the next architecture boundary.
openRisks: Codex app-server protocol remains experimental; keep exec fallback and do not assume thread resume across app restarts.
SQLite must not store OAuth or Codex credentials.
Large artifacts, screenshots, and recordings should live in a blob store with DB metadata, not in SQLite rows.
Screen streaming and recording need CPU, memory, retention, and user-consent guardrails before daily use.
iterations.summary: Iteration 3 completed the planned durable product-state sprint set. The daemon now owns SQLite storage with migrations, app-data/blob paths, WAL/foreign-key setup, runtime storage diagnostics, `/storage/health`, a no-secret app-setting boundary, and smoke coverage. Durable session tabs/trash are implemented with daemon session snapshots, SQLite-backed messages, internal renderer tabs, New chat session creation, branch-to-new-session behavior, restorable trash, and per-session model/reasoning/mode restoration. The artifact/activity ledger persists tool output and app-server file-change events as blob-backed artifacts with snapshots, text diffs where possible, click-to-open file entries, chat and trash artifact viewers, one-line activity summaries, and an activity detail popover. Vision now has a popup for snapshot capture, WebM recording, and Agent screen streaming; recordings preserve daemon metadata plus blob storage, Agent stream sends low-frequency live frames to the Vision snapshot endpoint without storing a video file, and mascot/status hooks reflect offline, working, recording, and streaming states. This is not the completion of the product-wide /goal; it only closes the Iteration 3 sprint set. Remaining work continues in Iteration 4.

iterations.label: Backlog Closure And Dogfood Polish
iterations.goal: Continue Codex Widget product development through repeated vibe-iterate sprints until the categorized dogfooding backlog is closed: UI polish, session/tab behavior, Agent widget awareness, artifact rendering/version UX, Vision streaming/voice foundations, PTY popup behavior, mascot/persona behavior, and durable runtime/provider history gaps.
iterations.carryover: The product owner clarified that the prior /goal meant repeated /vibe-iterate execution for all remaining task groups, not stopping after Iteration 3. Iter-3 delivered the SQLite/session/artifact/Vision foundations; iter-4 carries forward the visible dogfooding backlog plus deeper runtime/context/product-surface gaps.
openRisks: The external goal tracker was prematurely marked complete and cannot be reverted by the available tool; this iteration history is the durable correction.
Codex app-server protocol remains experimental; keep exec fallback and avoid assuming durable thread resume until explicitly implemented.
Vision screen streaming needs dogfooding for CPU, memory, cadence, privacy, and retention behavior.
Artifact version preservation must avoid data loss while keeping blob storage growth bounded.
Future custom theme/mascot/module platform work should remain bounded to data and persona foundations in this iteration.
iterations.summary: Iteration 4 completed its planned dogfooding polish sprint set. Sprint 01 completed visible UI/session polish; Sprint 02 added daemon-owned widget capability context per Agent turn; Sprint 03 upgraded artifact surfaces with file type icons, text/image previews, version metadata, versioned open requests, and reusable chat/trash artifact browser coverage; Sprint 04 clarified Vision recording vs Agent screen sharing, added cadence/duration controls, retained consent/retention details in daemon stream metadata, added outside-click dismissal, and added a Web Speech API voice prompt input boundary; Sprint 05 added a PTY guide/popout entry point and injected Default Dog mascot persona/tone into Agent widget context. Remaining follow-up should continue in a new iteration focused on durable runtime thread rebinding, provider snapshot history UI, and dogfood-driven resource tuning.

iterations.label: Runtime Rebinding And Provider History Closure
iterations.goal: Close the remaining feasible Codex Widget backlog through vibe-iterate: durable app-server runtime thread rebinding per restored/switched session, provider snapshot history UI, Vision resource and retention tuning, and a final completion audit.
iterations.carryover: Iter-4 completed the visible dogfooding polish set and left a narrow remaining backlog: durable app-server thread rebinding, provider snapshot history UI, and Vision resource tuning. The product owner now asked to continue all possible remaining work through vibe-iterate.
openRisks: Codex app-server protocol remains experimental; stale persisted thread ids fall back safely, but cross-process resume behavior needs dogfooding/live protocol validation.
Vision screen sharing has bounded defaults and diagnostics, but final CPU/memory tuning depends on longer real use.
Browser store account submission remains intentionally deferred until after dogfooding.
iterations.summary: Iteration 5 completed the remaining feasible non-dogfood backlog. Sprint 01 implemented session-aware Codex app-server thread rebinding with stale-thread retry/clear behavior. Sprint 02 implemented redacted provider snapshot history in daemon ledger snapshots and the Activity detail popover. Sprint 03 tuned Vision resource/retention behavior with in-flight frame throttling, skipped-frame diagnostics, duplicate-stop prevention, cleanup on provider terminal events, and effective guardrail metadata. Sprint 04 refreshed roadmap, milestone, handoff, session-log, and report state and classified remaining work as dogfood-dependent or externally deferred.

iterations.label: Renderer Architecture Refactor
iterations.goal: Refactor the oversized React renderer into a maintainable frontend structure without changing widget behavior.
iterations.carryover: Dogfooding exposed that the renderer had grown into a single oversized App.tsx plus single CSS file. The refactor keeps the daemon/session/runtime architecture intact and only changes frontend organization.
openRisks: App.tsx still owns complex daemon protocol and native window orchestration; future feature sprints should continue extracting focused hooks when behavior changes.
Renderer visual behavior should be dogfooded because this sprint intentionally avoided redesigning UI behavior.
iterations.summary: Iteration 6 split renderer UI structure by responsibility: App.tsx now focuses on state/effects and daemon/native orchestration; titlebar, system strip, mode tabs, settings, conversation, prompt/model controls, session strip, activity log, terminal, Vision menu, artifacts, markdown, floating tooltip, and interaction UI live under src/renderer/components; shared constants/types moved into config.ts and types.ts; behavior helpers moved into hooks and utils; and the monolithic CSS file is now an import manifest over scoped partials. Verification passed lint, renderer build, renderer chat smoke, diff check, strict UTF-8 decoding, and mojibake scan.

iterations.label: Dogfood UI Motion Polish
iterations.goal: Apply dogfood UI polish for trash artifact alignment, Activity footer height, and mascot motion.
iterations.carryover: After the renderer structure refactor, the product owner identified three concrete UI corrections: artifact icon placement in trash, Activity footer height, and replacing CSS bounce mascot effects with frame-based motion from the existing mascot asset.
openRisks: Product-owner review rejected the generated single-pose mascot sprite as a proxy implementation. It must not be treated as accepted mascot motion.
Mascot motion needs a consensus step and real authored pose/expression/state animation assets before another implementation pass.
The generated sprite asset adds about 1.69 MB to renderer assets and should be removed or replaced when the real mascot motion direction is selected.
iterations.summary: Iteration 7 moved the trash artifact icon next to the count and reduced the Activity footer from the old 76px reserve to 52px. The generated 9-frame mascot sprite was later rejected by product-owner review because it derives from one static pose and does not meet the intent of a genuinely moving mascot. Future mascot motion work must begin with consensus on acceptance criteria and use real authored motion assets. The previous smoke coverage only proves the sprite path exists; it is not acceptance evidence for animation quality.

iterations.label: Vision Context Interface
iterations.goal: Build the Vision Context Interface from docs/plans/vision-context-interface-handoff.md end-to-end: a daemon-side module that converts screen/browser/user capture into TaskCapsule markdown plus selected Codex app-server localImage inputs, without ever sending raw WebM/audio to app-server.
iterations.carryover: Iter-7 dogfood UI motion work is no longer the active implementation focus. The product owner supplied docs/plans/vision-context-interface-handoff.md as the authoritative handoff for a new Vision Context feature iteration. The durable decisions are that raw WebM/audio are temporary processing material only, the model-visible product is TaskCapsule text plus selected localImage evidence, and deterministic interfaces should precede real ASR complexity.
openRisks: Codex app-server video input is not available; the implementation must stay on UserInput text/image variants.
Raw media deletion must run on both successful and failed processing paths.
Real local ASR production support may require a sidecar or installed model and should remain optional behind an interface until dogfooding validates the backend choice.
Destructive low-confidence requests require clarification rather than silent action.
iterations.summary: Iteration 8 implemented the Vision Context Interface MVP. The daemon now has src/daemon/vision-context with TaskCapsule schemas, capture session timeline, evidence graph, reference and intent resolvers, capsule markdown rendering, retention/raw deletion policy, app-server UserInput adapter, built-in screen/browser/terminal adapters, and placeholder IDE/document/accessibility adapters. src/daemon/transcription now provides transcript/audio schemas, mock ASR, sidecar ASR boundary, VAD fixture helper, lexicon correction, action-slot confidence, and clarification policy. The shared protocol includes visionContext start/event/stop/cancel plus progress/capsule/sent/error events, AgentRequest supports appServerInput overrides, Codex app-server turns accept localImage inputs, and the renderer starts/stops Vision Context around Share with Agent. Smoke coverage verifies capsule generation, pointer/no-pointer/temporal resolver behavior, raw media deletion, lexicon correction, destructive clarification, and fake app-server localImage delivery.

iterations.label: Browser Action Interface
iterations.goal: Implement the Browser Action Interface from docs/plans/browser-action-interface-handoff.md: a daemon-side browser observe-plan-act-verify actuator with typed actions, target resolution, safety policy, extension/native integration, renderer approval, app-server smoke coverage, audit logging, and future adapter scaffolds.
iterations.carryover: Iter-8 completed Vision Context. The product owner now wants the browser actuator layer that can later connect to Windows computer-use. The authoritative handoff is docs/plans/browser-action-interface-handoff.md. Keep arbitrary JavaScript out of the default path; build typed, verified, auditable browser actions first.
openRisks: Live semantic dogfood on real websites is still needed before claiming Windows computer-use parity or UX-level browser automation acceptance.
CDP, Playwright, and native desktop adapters are scaffolds/placeholders until a future expansion sprint.
Arbitrary JavaScript/evaluate remains deferred to a future full_control_dev capability with visible code preview, approval, audit logging, and credential safeguards.
Chrome/Edge restricted pages may remain unsupported until CDP/native desktop adapters are added.
iterations.summary: Iteration 9 implemented the Browser Action Interface MVP. The daemon now has src/daemon/browser-action with normalized observations, stable element ids, element graph, target resolver, safety policy, typed action queue/executor model, result verifier, audit helpers, extension adapter, and future CDP/Playwright/native desktop placeholders. The DOM extension preserves snapshot behavior while adding structured interactive elements and typed action execution. Shared protocol and daemon handlers support browserAction start/observe/execute/cancel, extension poll/result HTTP endpoints, approval UI reuse, progress/result/error events, renderer Activity visibility, app-server widget-context visibility, and smoke coverage for resolver/safety/approval/extension-result/audit paths. This is explicitly incomplete for the production-level Browser Action goal because CDP/Playwright/native adapter implementations, full_control_dev evaluate, stronger adapter diagnostics, and live dogfood evidence remain open.

The product owner clarified that the original goal was production-level interface completion, not MVP closure. This iteration treats iter-9 as a partial baseline and implements or precisely blocks the remaining production adapter surfaces.

First-class Browser Action custom tool integration remains BLOCKED on a stable Codex app-server custom tool/client-tool contract; daemon protocol simulation and widget context cover current agent visibility.
Restricted browser pages remain subject to browser/extension/CDP security boundaries and should report unsupported state rather than bypassing protections.
iterations.summary: Iteration 10 completed the Browser Action production expansion beyond iter-9 MVP: adapter registry/status, direct controlled-adapter execution, stale reobserve/retry, functional Playwright and CDP adapters, bounded native desktop diagnostics with explicit UIA BLOCKED record, full_control_dev evaluate approval/hash/timeout/result-limit/credential safeguards, adapter/evaluate/native smokes, and real semantic dogfood evidence.

Windows UI Automation executable browser chrome control remains BLOCKED on a scoped helper; the control surface should expose native diagnostics without implying executable fallback support.

The widget now has a Vision-like Browser Action popup anchored to the Browser mode button, direct UI commands normalize into BrowserActionPlan execution through the existing daemon safety/approval/adapter/verify/audit pipeline, natural-language Browser prompt execution remains intact, informational Browser Action questions are no longer misclassified, and dogfood evidence now covers direct UI observe/read/safe-action plus prompt-driven and adapter-driven paths.

iterations.label: Browser Extension Bridge UX
iterations.goal: Complete docs/plans/browser-extension-bridge-handoff.md end-to-end: convert the DOM snapshot extension into a Codex Widget Browser Bridge with popup/settings, badge heartbeat, explicit site permission, command-first polling/execution, widget status visibility, simplified Browser UI, smokes, and dogfood evidence.

iterations.summary: Iteration 13 completed the Browser Extension Bridge UX refactor. The extension icon now opens a Browser Bridge popup, badge states show OFF/IDLE/RUN/ASK/ERR, daemon base URL and bridge settings are configurable, the service worker heartbeat/status is visible to daemon and widget, approved-site auto-observe plus command polling removes the manual snapshot step, site permission and restricted-page states are explicit, Browser mode foregrounds bridge status while moving adapters/debug under diagnostics, extension/store/privacy/review copy is updated, and verification passed lint, build:web, smoke, smoke:all, Browser Action adapter/control smokes, extension/native-host/DOM/app-server smokes, Browser Bridge smoke/dogfood, Browser Action E2E dogfood, and cargo check.

iterations.label: Browser Action Semantic Target Pipeline
iterations.goal: Benchmark the Vision Context evidence graph/reference resolver/intent resolver structure and complete the Browser Action natural-language intent plus DOM target-resolution pipeline so Korean commands such as 새 채팅 눌러줘 normalize, resolve, pass safety, and reach the extension action path reliably.
iterations.carryover: Iter-13 made Browser Bridge snapshotless in the UX, but prompt execution could still fail on Korean target commands because prompt planning used regex-only target text and the resolver treated broad DOM containers as nearly equal alternatives to the intended actionable element.
openRisks: The installed unpacked browser extension must be reloaded after service-worker changes before the live browser uses the HTTP-first auto-observe path.
First-class app-server custom Browser Action tools remain BLOCKED on a stable Codex app-server client-tool contract; this iteration continues to use daemon-owned deterministic prompt routing.
Live site DOMs can still produce genuinely ambiguous targets; side-effect actions should continue to clarify when no actionable candidate exceeds the safety threshold.
iterations.summary: Iteration 14 completed a Vision Context-style Browser Action semantic target pipeline. Added a dedicated Browser Action intent resolver and target lexicon, normalized Korean command suffixes such as 눌러줘, expanded exact/alias/compact/token matching for Korean and English target labels, capped non-actionable container candidates so links/buttons/inputs win over broad page regions, added prompt/resolver smoke coverage for 새 채팅 눌러줘, and hardened the Browser Bridge auto-observe transport to post snapshots directly to the daemon before falling back to native host transport.

iterations.label: Semantic Interface
iterations.goal: Complete docs/plans/semantic-interface-handoff.md end-to-end: reusable daemon-side semantic decision boundary with type surface, golden trace/replay, transition grammar, operating profiles, redacted durable traces, Browser Action shadow/advisory/live gate, Vision read/locate conformance, adversarial fixtures, docs, and verification.
iterations.carryover: Iter-14 improved Browser Action prompt intent/target resolution, but that semantic logic remains Browser Action-specific. Iter-15 extracts a reusable semantic-interface module while preserving Browser Action safety and using shadow/advisory phases before low-risk live adoption.
openRisks: Terminal, Workspace, Screen/OCR, and Windows UI Automation adapters remain future consumers of the semantic-interface contract; Browser Action and Vision Context are the completed v1 conformance targets.
Statistical calibration remains deferred until a held-out dogfood trace set exists; v1 uses evidence-profile gating plus top-vs-runner-up margin.
LLM enrichment remains logged-only future work and must not feed deterministic ranker scores without a separate typed validator.
iterations.summary: Iteration 15 completed the reusable semantic-interface module from docs/plans/semantic-interface-handoff.md. The daemon now has a package-like src/daemon/semantic-interface boundary with v1 type contracts, ontology/version constants, intent frames, deterministic hypotheses/ranking, transition grammar, operating profiles, pure safety predicates, trace/replay, redacted durable trace projection, generic alias lexicon, Browser Action and Vision Context adapters, typed/untyped/adversarial golden trace harness, and dogfood evidence. Browser Action keeps execution feature-owned but can use semantic target resolution as a low-risk live gate with redacted trace metadata; Vision Context read/locate conformance works without core type or ranker changes.

iterations.label: Semantic Interface View Graph And Memory
iterations.goal: Complete docs/plans/semantic-interface-handoff.md and docs/plans/semantic-memory-handoff.md: typed evidence packets, Browser View Graph evidence, immutable Semantic Memory read sets, clarification/correction feedback, live Browser Action memory integration, user controls, smokes, and dogfood evidence.
iterations.carryover: Iter-15 completed the reusable semantic-interface baseline. User follow-up required the remaining typed evidence-packet refinements, View Graph grounding, and Semantic Memory layer so repeated ambiguity/correction can improve future target resolution without bypassing safety.
openRisks: Dedicated ranked-choice clarification card UX can still be refined; current implementation records unresolved cases, exposes input/approval surfaces, and keeps Browser Action safety-owned clarification behavior.
Node's built-in SQLite module is still experimental in the current runtime and prints an ExperimentalWarning in some dogfood scripts.
Memory improves ranking only after fresh observed candidates pass hard gates; it intentionally does not override permissions or low-confidence side-effect safety.
iterations.summary: Iteration 16 completed the Semantic Interface refinement and Semantic Memory implementation. Semantic hypotheses now carry typed basis-point evidence packets, ranker traces, candidate-generation provenance, pairwise margins, and target fingerprints. Browser observations now include View Graph identity/nodes/edges and Semantic Interface maps view regions, roles, and relations into ranking evidence. Semantic Memory adds local SQLite-backed nodes/edges/unresolved/feedback storage, redaction/hash helpers, immutable MemoryReadSet projections, ranker memory axes, live Browser Action read-set integration with safety metadata provenance, unresolved-case recording, daemon report/read/reset/settings endpoints, renderer Settings controls, `npm run smoke:semantic-memory`, and `npm run dogfood:semantic-memory` evidence.

iterations.label: Browser Action Runtime Closure
iterations.goal: Continue Browser Action/Semantic Interface work in the user-requested order 2 -> 3 -> 1 -> 6 -> 7 -> 5: View Graph runtime audit and gap closure, Semantic Interface/Memory live audit, prompt-driven Browser Action failure fixes, dogfood matrix refresh, agent-friendly refactor follow-up, and Browser Action UX cleanup.
iterations.carryover: Iter-16 completed View Graph and Semantic Memory implementation, but live Browser Action dogfood still fails on dynamic page transitions and ambiguous Korean browser commands. This iteration treats the previous implementation as a baseline to audit and harden, not as sufficient acceptance.
openRisks: Live Browser Bridge behavior depends on the installed unpacked extension being reloaded after service-worker changes.
Dynamic pages can change URL/query/view identity between observe and execute; expected-source guards must distinguish stale-source risk from intentional step-to-step navigation.
Semantic Memory must improve ranking only through typed read-set evidence and must not bypass Browser Action safety or permissions.
iterations.summary: Iteration 17 completed the requested 2 -> 3 -> 1 -> 6 -> 7 -> 5 pass. Browser Action prompt execution now recovers from extension expected-source URL/tab/window mismatch by refreshing the active observation and retrying the affected step once. Browser Bridge poll requests update daemon-visible active-tab status. Representative content resolution now rejects utility/profile/category/comment anchors and prefers article-like content links. Browser prompt failures, clarification, and pending-extension states render clearer user-facing messages instead of opaque execution receipts. Verification covered lint, build, Browser Action/Bridge/Semantic smokes, and dogfood evidence scripts.

Shadow DOM, cross-origin iframes, virtualized lists, and highly visual/icon-only UIs may need later adapter or Vision Context fusion.
